Lemma
[nearest point and separating half-space] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0060, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0061 1. ch10:10.35–10.36\group Convex geometry

Every point outside a closed convex set has a unique nearest boundary point, depending continuously on the point (and on a continuously varying convex set), and the hyperplane perpendicular to the joining segment separates the point from the set.
Proof

\sketch Existence follows from coercivity of distance on a closed set. If two nearest points existed, their midpoint would be strictly closer by the parallelogram identity. The same identity plus compactness proves continuity. For the nearest point $V$ to $W$, convexity implies $\langle X-V,W-V\rangle \le 0$ for all $X$ in the set, which is the separating half-space.

□
